title: Config Sweeper: Delta-Prober evaluation for batching & KV policy tradeoffs
creator: Ravi Singh
description: Build and run a deterministic evaluation harness ("Delta-Prober") that sweeps batching and KV-cache policy parameters to map the latency-vs-quality frontier and produce actionable defaults, alert thresholds, and automated rollback criteria. This ticket covers the experiment design, datasets, metrics, automation for nightly regression detection, and handoff artifacts for Console dashboards and alerting playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Full sweep run produces a CSV matrix of config combinations with latency and quality metrics stratified by prompt cohort and sequence length
Latency-vs-quality frontier plots for each model variant (PDF + interactive) stored in runtime-evals-2025 Drive folder
A recommended 'safe default' config and 'cost-first' config with clear expected P50/P95 and median quality delta
Regression detectors implemented that will raise an alert in the Console if any config degrades golden-set quality by >1.5% or increases P95 latency by >20%
Canary rollout plan and automated rollback hooks described and tested in staging
datasets: golden_prompts_v2 (2k curated prompts with human quality labels; stratified by domain and hallucination sensitivity)
synthetic_prefix_continuations (5k prompts generated to probe prefix caching effects)
production-sampled-1h (privacy-sampled, token-subsampled traces from January; used for latency distribution estimation)
customer_cohort_A (anonymized 500 sessions for domain-specific sensitivity checks)
metrics: quality.regression_rate (fraction of golden prompts where score falls > threshold)
plan_steps: 1) Implement Delta-Prober harness in runtime-evals repo: config-driven runner that enumerates matrix and emits standard CSV rows
2) Wire runner to staging model endpoints and to an isolated perf cluster to capture stable latency percentiles
3) Run baseline sweep for two model variants to seed frontier visualization (expected runtime ~12 hrs for full matrix on perf cluster)
4) Compute quality deltas vs baseline using golden_prompts_v2 and semantic similarity; flag anomalies for manual triage
5) Produce frontier plots and an algorithm to pick pareto-optimal configs given customer SLO weights
6) Add nightly scheduled sweep (reduced matrix) and regression detectors integrated with Console alerting
7) Document recommended defaults and add canary/rollback hooks to deployment runbooks
rollout_plan: staging: run full sweep and validate artifacts in Drive and dashboard
canary-1: deploy chosen config to 1% of traffic with verbose tracing enabled for 24h
canary-10: expand to 10% if no regressions; continue to monitor for 72h
gradual: ramp to 50% over one week with automated checks at each step
rollback: auto-rollback trigger if golden_set_quality drops >1.5% or P95 latency increases >20% for >1h
notes: We intentionally separate prefix-only vs full kvcache to isolate initial-token benefits from long-run KV pressure
Synthetic prefixes should include adversarial patterns to surface caching correctness issues (tokenization boundary shifts, early-termination differences)
Expect different optimal configs by sequence length; the final Console 'policy selector' should be able to switch configs by route/seq_len bucket
Coordinate with Observability (Marta Kim) for custom traces and with SDK team (Diego Torres) for tracing hooks
